A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OAR research work. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–G support a reliable comparison, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic, IHDP, ACIC 2016, and HC-MNIST experiments, including comparisons with other regularization strategies and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports updated HC-MNIST results over more runs.

M1.justification: The OAR noise, dropout, and RKHS formulations, debiasing corrections, rescaling, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The expanded kernel-method description and main-text discussion of debiasing-term clipping were already documented in v1's appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic, IHDP, ACIC 2016, and HC-MNIST tasks and data-generating settings. IHDP moves into the main experimental discussion while synthetic results move to Appendix G; neither is new coverage.

E2.justification: Constant regularization remains the primary comparator for DR-, R-, and IVW-learners. Tables 7 and 8 retain the same trimming and Wasserstein/MMD balancing comparisons for DR- and R-learners.

E3.justification: Appendices E–F retain the data splits, preprocessing, architectures, training budgets, hyperparameter tuning, regularization settings, and rPEHE metric. The increased HC-MNIST repeated-run count concerns statistical reporting rather than a changed evaluation design.

E4.justification: The same regularization-strength and function comparisons, synthetic/IHDP sweeps, and runtime analysis are retained. HC-MNIST results are refreshed, but no new ablation question, robustness scenario, error analysis, or case study is introduced.

E5.justification: HC-MNIST reporting increases from 10 to 30 runs in Tables 3, 6, and 8. Tables 3 and 6 newly distinguish significant differences at alpha = 0.05 from merely positive or negative differences. Mean/standard-deviation reporting and other benchmarks' run counts remain unchanged; the significance test is not identified.

E6.justification: The updated HC-MNIST summaries revise values and some rankings in Tables 3, 6, and 8. For IVW/dropout at p = 0.5 in Table 6, squared-multiplicative OAR/dOAR means change from 0.891/0.925 to 0.820/0.810, reversing their ranking. These are updated 30-run estimates, not evidence of a method improvement. Other benchmark and runtime results are retained.

T1.justification: v2 adds Proposition 7 and an RKHS excess-risk derivation in Appendices C and D.3, extending beyond v1's kernel-solution results. It also revises Proposition 5's variance formula and penalty-allocation argument, corrects its main-text constant-variance assumption from pseudo-outcome to outcome, and strengthens the general overlap assumption to a uniform bound.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding paragraph retain the same central contributions: overlap-dependent regularization, parametric and nonparametric implementations, debiasing that preserves Neyman-orthogonality, and improved low-overlap CATE estimation. The added theoretical material does not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds reasons to prefer multiplicative regularization and the DR-learner, including an explanation of possible over-regularization with R-/IVW-learners. Section 4.1 qualifies exact implicit/explicit equivalence to linear models, and Section 5.3 expands discussion of the variance assumption. The existing low-overlap/low-heterogeneity limitation remains.

D1.justification: The stated code and tuned-hyperparameter access location changes from an anonymous repository to the named GitHub repository. Appendix E.2 adds computational-complexity information. Architectures, hyperparameters, hardware, pseudocode, and clipping details were already supplied in v1.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to Frauen et al. (2025) and Hess et al. (2026) concerning longitudinal meta-learners. The main research positioning remains unchanged. Several other reference changes, including Kennedy and Luedtke, update publication information for already cited works.

P1.justification: v2 makes local language edits, promotes existing kernel material into Section 5.4, exchanges the IHDP and synthetic experimental discussions, and integrates the conclusion into Section 6. It adds ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements and conference headers; most existing prose and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The existing IHDP and synthetic plots exchange main-text/appendix placement and Figure 2/4 numbering, with corresponding resizing. HC-MNIST table colors and legends now encode significance. Figures, table structures, and the overall visual style are otherwise largely retained.

improvement.justification: The expanded HC-MNIST repetitions and significance markings improve empirical reporting, while corrections to Proposition 5 reduce inconsistencies in the theoretical explanation. The added kernel analysis and methodological discussion improve completeness. These gains are limited by the unnamed significance-test procedure and the informal final variance-comparison argument in the new RKHS proof; a substantial overall improvement is not established.
